snip.t: The resultant “shift to the right” of the oxygen dissociation curve reduces the affinity of hemoglobin for oxygen and results in more complete transfer of oxygen to the tissues.\n

The same shift in the oxygen dissociation curve can also occur at high altitude.\nHigher levels of erythropoietin (EPO) and consequent increased RBC production by the bone marrow further assist the body to adapt.

qs.q: The 'Oxygen Dissociation Curve' of hemoglobin shifts to the RIGHT in which of the following conditions?
o: Increased pH level in the blood
Increased PCO2 level in the blood
qs.e: A right shift (reduced affinity, easier O2 offloading) is caused by increased H+ (lower pH), increased CO2, increased temperature, and increased 2,3-BPG.
